A single shape cut from black paper with scissors: the outline of a naval officer of 1817 seen straight on, facing the viewer square-on, full length from head to feet, standing centred and symmetrical with his feet planted apart. His head is bare and perfectly smooth, a plain solid oval sitting on his neck, with nothing on it and nothing in it. Broad square shoulders, a fringed epaulette sitting proud on each shoulder, a high standing collar, and a long plain coat falling straight to below the knee. His right arm is raised high, holding a wooden gavel well above his head and clear of it against open white. His left hand holds an unrolled scroll out to the side. The whole shape stands centred with generous white space on every side.

The shape is one single unbroken mass of solid black, as flat as paper. Every feature is carried by its outer edge alone: solid black head, solid black collar, solid black epaulettes, solid black scroll, solid black coat. The head is empty black: no eyes, no nose, no mouth, no ears, no chin line, no hair, no hat, no helmet, no cap.
